result.title: Beyond the Point Mass: Acceptance-Derived Weights and Distributional Losses for Speculative Decoding
result.summary: In speculative decoding, a lightweight draft model proposes tokens that the target model verifies in parallel, speeding up generation without changing the target distribution. D-PACE (Wu et al., 2026) trains such drafters with a loss that weights each position by its contribution to the expected accepted length. Both its weights and its cross-entropy (CE) loss use only the draft's probability of the recorded target token, treating the target as a point mass. Under rejection sampling, however, a sampled draft token is accepted with probability equal to the overlap of the draft and target distributions, one minus their total variation (TV). We derive D-PAL (Dynamic Position-wise Acceptance Loss) from the exact expected accepted length, using this overlap as the acceptance signal. This yields overlap-based position weights with log acceptance (LA) as the per-position loss, and the objective reduces to D-PACE for a point-mass target. Since the weights are detached, any per-position loss can replace LA in practice. We show that forward KL divergence and Rényi divergence of order 1/2 match or exceed LA, and that Rényi-1/2 provably bounds the true acceptance rate from above and below. Replacing CE with Rényi-1/2 improves acceptance length under both D-PACE's weights and ours. On six benchmarks with a Qwen3-4B target, D-PAL raises mean acceptance length over D-PACE from 4.50 to 4.57 at T=0 and from 4.20 to 4.28 at T=1, and consistently achieves higher throughput at both temperatures.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从投机解码的期望接受长度出发推导 D-PAL：以 draft 与 target 分布的重叠（1−TV）作为每位置的接受权重，并用 log acceptance、forward KL、Rényi-1/2 等分布损失替代点质量交叉熵，在多个基准上提升平均接受长度与吞吐。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按「对期望接受长度的贡献」给各位置加权、并以分布重叠作为接收信号的思路，可能为 latent 推理轨迹中逐步监督分配与草稿—验证式并行生成提供可核查的损失设计线索，但对象是纯文本解码加速，与视觉推理无直接关联。
